2026-11-09.text: The satellite looked again on 9 Nov, 12 days after landfall. The numbers are likely to change as more radar pictures arrive. Cyclone Murasu (1 to 3 Nov) probably also put water on the land. The Godavari river peak (about 2 Nov) probably did too. This radar picture shows all of it together, not Cyclone Arnab alone. Radar points to about 84 square km of new open water (61 to 108 with other settings). That is more than ten times a normal fortnight.
2026-11-09.headline: More land is probably flooded than on the last radar pass.

2026-10-28.text: NISAR looked at the coast on 28 Oct, the day Cyclone Arnab reached land. Radar shows only small patches of likely new open water, too few to call any mandal flooded. Radar points to about 8 square km of new open water (5 to 13 with other settings). That is about 4 times a normal fortnight.
2026-10-28.headline: No mandal looks probably flooded in this radar picture.
